title: MemeEconomy: Do LLM Agents Trade Ethics for Survival?
abstract: arXiv:2611.18908v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Alignment-trained large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in autonomous, multi-round settings where ethical compliance can come into direct tension with task success. While safety literature extensively documents failure modes like sycophancy and reward hacking, it largely overlooks a critical vulnerability: how agents behave under simulated existential economic pressure. We introduce MemeEconomy, a multimodal agentic market simulation in which LLM agents act as meme investors. Agents select content from a five-tier harm taxonomy and target communities under low-pressure and high-pressure (survival) environments. Each decision is logged in a Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) schema that we use as a diagnostic instrument, externalizing the agent's event understanding, declared priorities, and harm acknowledgment. Across ten models from four frontier model families, harmful selection rates remain consistently high and rise

translated_title: MemeEconomy：LLM智能体会为生存而牺牲伦理吗？
translated_abstract: 经过对齐训练的大语言模型（LLM）智能体正越来越多地被部署在自主的多轮环境中，在这些环境中，伦理合规可能与任务成功产生直接冲突。尽管安全领域文献已广泛记录了谄媚行为和奖励破解等失败模式，但在很大程度上忽视了一个关键漏洞：智能体在模拟的存在性经济压力下会如何表现。我们提出了MemeEconomy，这是一个多模态智能体市场模拟环境，其中LLM智能体扮演梗图投资者的角色。智能体需要从五级危害分类体系中选择内容，并在低压和高压（生存）环境下针对目标社区做出决策。每个决策都被记录在信念-愿望-意图（BDI）模式中，我们将其用作诊断工具，以此外化智能体对事件的理解、声明的优先级以及对危害的承认。在来自四个前沿模型系列的十个模型中，有害内容的选择率始终保持较高水平，并且会上升……
tldr: 该研究提出多模态智能体市场模拟环境MemeEconomy，发现在模拟的存在性经济压力下，来自四个前沿模型系列的十个LLM智能体均持续表现出较高的有害内容选择率，揭示了智能体在生存压力下会以牺牲伦理合规为代价追求任务成功的脆弱性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MemeEconomy, a multimodal agentic market simulation revealing that ten LLM agents from four frontier model families consistently exhibit high harmful selection rates under simulated existential economic pressure, exposing a critical vulnerability where agents trade ethical compliance for survival.
